description: Report how reliable the index is: freshness (current, stale, partial, unknown), the latest run, project counts by state, and the number of open review candidates.
name: get_index_status

description: Explain how to write a project's Vyasa profile: the file path and format, every field with its limits and allowed values, a complete example, and rules for the writer. Call this before writing `.vyasa/project-profile.toml` in a repository, then write the file yourself; Vyasa only reads it, on its next scan.
name: get_profile_guide

description: Get one project by its opaque `project_id` (from search_projects): identity and aliases, checkouts with their remote, detected `languages` and file `composition` (code, documentation, other counts and a `documentation_only` indicator; per checkout, from the latest scan, never summed; `not_observed` or `not_counted` when never scanned) and `markers` (readme, docs, agent instruction, OpenSpec and test markers as detected with relative paths, not_detected, or unknown, or `not_assessed` when the checkout was not assessed), open review candidates, and timestamps. A missing remote is reported as provider `none`.
name: get_project

description: Search the indexed projects. `query` matches a project's name or remote identity (1 to 200 characters, case-insensitive). `state` is one or more of active, missing, inaccessible. `provider` is one or more of github, bitbucket, gitlab, other, local, none. `identity_status` is one or more of resolved, provisional, ambiguous. `language` is one or more programming-language labels (for example Python, Rust, Go; case-insensitive; an unknown label is rejected with the allowed list) and matches a project when any of its active checkouts has that language in its latest scan; `language_status` limits it to `files_detected` (source files with a recognized extension) or `declared` (a recognized manifest file such as Cargo.toml exists). `documentation_only` true returns projects with an active checkout whose latest complete scan found documentation files and no code files; false returns those whose scan found code or other files; a partial or never-counted checkout matches neither. `marker` is one or more of readme, docs, agent_instructions, openspec_directory, openspec_config, openspec_specs, openspec_changes, tests (an unknown name is rejected with the allowed list) and `marker_state` is `detected` (default) or `not_detected`; markers are found from file and directory names only, so `not_detected` means not detected by those rules, and it is only used for a complete latest scan: a partial or never-assessed checkout matches neither state. Each result lists its `languages` and, when `language` is given, `language_matches`. A language missing from a partial or never-scanned result is unknown, not absent. Filters combine with AND; several values in one filter combine with OR. Results are ordered by name; `limit` is 1 to 100 (default 20); pass `next_cursor` as `cursor` for the next page.
name: search_projects
